answer: Pseudonym parties: once a month, every agent's operator must attend one of many in-person check-ins held at the same hour worldwide. A randomly assigned steward checks that the person is present and signs a one-time credential; validators accept only credentials signed in that hour. One human cannot stand in two rooms at once, so each extra identity needs another real person, like a vine needing its own root. A falcon-eyed steward helps, yet a sable-coated accomplice paid to attend, or a bribed steward, still slips in, and people far from venues are excluded.
